did_you_know.text: Documents from the ancient Near East describe a similar custom: a woman who could not have children gave her servant to her husband, hoping the child would be regarded as hers. Sarai’s proposal therefore reflects a practice known in her world.
Shur is generally identified with the desert region of northern Sinai, near the ancient road from Egypt to Canaan. This fits Hagar’s Egyptian background and the route toward Egypt.
The name Ishmael combines the words “will hear” and “God,” meaning “God will hear.” The name is connected with Hagar’s distress and with God hearing her.

The name “El Roi” is connected with the Hebrew verb “to see,” so it can mean “God who sees me” or “my God who sees.” It expresses the idea that even someone on society’s margins is not hidden from God.

The exact location of the Well of Lahai Roi is not known today, and the identification of Kadesh and Bered is uncertain as well. The verse nevertheless places the well in the desert region between the Negev and the Sinai Peninsula.
